sources.inventory: f16net-aim9, f16net-aim120, f16net-tanks, w-f16-arm, sufa-at, inferred, fi-pathfinder

notes.positions: each station's place on the wing as the Loadout screen names it: 1 / 9 the wingtip rails, 2 / 8 outboard, 3 / 7 mid, 4 / 6 inboard (the wet stations), 5 the targeting pod's chin hardpoint under the right intake (the real jet's 5R; the centreline is not used; inferred from the F-16's station numbering), 10 the navigation pod's chin hardpoint under the left intake (the real jet's 5L, numbered after the wing's nine: the engine's pylon J)
notes.labels: the chin hardpoints' real names, 5R (the sim's 5) and 5L (the sim's 10), shown in place of their numbers: the F-16's navigation pod on 5L (f16net-lantirn), the targeting pod on the other (inferred, modern-iaf/docs/research/pods.md §2.3)
notes.lateral_limit_kgm: the F-16's maximum allowable asymmetric (rolling) moment, 25,020 ft-lb (3,459 kg·m), as a forum quotes the flight manual's stores limitations (bms-asym; the manual itself not seen, so inferred); the Sufa's and the Barak's taken the same (inferred)
notes.lateral_limit_hard: false: the briefing warns and lets the jet fly (the manual forbids the take-off only when the roll trim cannot hold the moment, which the briefing does not know)
notes.allowed: the stores each station takes, by its real number. Sourced: the AIM-9 and the AIM-120 on 1 / 9, 2 / 8 and 3 / 7 (f16net-aim9, f16net-aim120); the GBU-31 on 3 / 7, one each, and the GBU-38 there two to a BRU-57/A (120.2 kg, l3h-bru57; f16net-jdam); three Mk 82 on a TER-9/A (47.6 kg, ter-9a) on 3 / 7, and on 4 / 6 (f16net-mk82, a forum: inferred; with tanks on 4 / 6 the real jet takes two on 3 / 7, not modelled); the 370 US gal tank on 4 / 6 (f16net-tanks) and the 600 US gal tank there (usaf-600). Inferred: the Python 5 on the AIM-9 rails 1 / 9 and 2 / 8 (a modified LAU-129; no station chart found); the Mk 83 and the Mk 84 one each on 3 / 7 and 4 / 6 (f16net-mk82 tells of four Mk 84); the SPICE 1000 / 2000 on 3 / 7 and 4 / 6 (no source gives their stations); the Delilah on none (dropped 2026-11-14: no cruise-missile flight class); the Sufa and the Barak the same (no source shows a difference). Each rack's rack_drag (drag index, flight-model.md §9.18) inferred as one of its stores' (a beam of about their cross-section). The laser-guided GBU-12, GBU-16 and GBU-10 (sufa-at) one each on 3 / 7 and 4 / 6, as the Mk 82 to Mk 84 bodies they are built on (inferred); the targeting pod (the Litening, sufa-at) on the right chin hardpoint (twz-litening: a chin station; the right side inferred from photos), the sim's station 5 (the user's yes to the pod and the laser bombs on the F-16s, 17 Nov 2026, avionics-plan.md §8.2); the Pathfinder navigation pod (AN/AAQ-20, the AN/AAQ-13's export version without the terrain-following radar) on the left chin hardpoint, 10 (5L): Israel's Pathfinders of 1992 (fi-pathfinder; the Barak's inferred), the F-16 carries the navigation pod on 5L (f16net-lantirn); carried, drawn and weighed only, its functions later (modern-iaf/docs/research/pods.md P7, P8)
notes.tail: the number the game draws on the player's Barak (shared/extra/models/f16/f16d.tail.json `number`, docs/aircraft-models.md §1.6: F-16D 034 of 109 Squadron, whose fin art and number the game draws on it; every other jet shows its own), so every screen shows the jet the player sees (the user, 2026-11-13, A31). 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-19 547, the FlightGear livery's, with 101 Squadron: 547 is a single-seat F-16C's and 101 flies F-16Cs only; the user, 19 Nov 2026: "Fix the Barak problem. Make sure the tail art match": 109 Squadron again, with a real F-16D of its own (the base file's `squadrons`)
notes.max_takeoff_kg: the F-16C/D Block 40/42's maximum take-off weight, 42,300 lb (19,187 kg), the same on f-16.net's Block 30/32 page (f16net-b30), where a reader's comment gives the Block 30 37,500 lb: the Block 30's kept the same (inferred); the player's Barak, 034, is a Block 30 (109 Squadron's, f-16.net), the sim's systems the Block 40's
notes.type: the F-16's type code; the airframe definition f16 is the Barak's
notes.model: none: the player's jet is drawn from its airframe definition (shared/extra/planes/f16/airframe.json)
notes.scale: 1: our models are built true size
notes.radius_m: half the span over the wingtip rails, 9.96 m
notes.strength: our damage scale's fighter (modern-iaf/docs/data-formats.md, damage scale)
notes.loadout.20mm: M61A1, 511 rounds (the F-16's; the two-seat Barak's count is not published, inferred the same)
notes.loadout.chaff: no public count found; 60 held until one is
notes.loadout.flare: no public count found; 60 held until one is
notes.pylons: an AIM-9M on each wingtip rail (stations 1 and 9, A and I): the F-16's wingtip rails carry its short-range missiles (w-f16); a 370 US gal tank on each wing's inboard station (stations 4 and 6, D and F; the F-16's wing tanks, f16net-tanks), carried on most flights (inferred); no other underwing stores in training (inferred); an AIM-9M on each underwing missile station, 2 / 8 (B, H) and 3 / 7 (C, G): the F-16 carries AIM-9s and AIM-120s there (f16net-aim9, f16net-aim120); on 2 / 8 the AIM-9M stands in for the IAF's Python (inferred), on 3 / 7 for an AIM-120, which the sim has no record of yet (stand-ins, inferred)
notes.inventory: the stores the briefing lists as the jet's, each its own record in data/db/weapons with its sourced weight and size: the AIM-9M, the Python 5, the AIM-120, the Mk 82, Mk 83 and Mk 84, the GBU-31 and GBU-38 JDAM, the SPICE 1000 and 2000, the 370 and 600 US gal tanks; no counts published
